notes: telmisartan-amlodipine marked no-uk-product: no UK SmPC/PIL/licence for the fixed-dose combination on emc or in the MHRA Products search index (ingredient, trade-name and substance-facet searches). The single-ingredient telmisartan and amlodipine entries remain usable. valsartan: no emc SmPC for 80 mg or 160 mg tablets (emc has 40/320 mg tablets and 40/80/160 mg capsules). Used the UK MHRA Products SmPC PDFs for valsartan 80 mg and 160 mg film-coated tablets (PL 34771/0020 and /0021); the clinic-linked emc 40 mg tablet SmPC (emc-8184) was checked (same 4.3/4.6 wording) and used only for the clearer paediatric maximum-dose table and oral-solution note. valsartan/hydrochlorothiazide: the clinic links emc-7746 and emc-5537 are the same combined SmPC text (80/12.5, 160/12.5, 160/25); emc-5537 used. emc-100496 (generic 160/12.5) not used. Within this SmPC, 4.2 says severe renal impairment GFR < 30 mL/min while 4.3 says creatinine clearance < 30 ml/min; the rule uses CrCl (4.3) and the renal section quotes both. Candesartan clinic links (emc-12850/12851) are the UK candesartan 8 mg/16 mg SmPCs; text identical apart from strength and lactose content. Aliskiren contraindication (with diabetes mellitus or GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) is in every ARB SmPC 4.3 but aliskiren is not in the master list, so it is recorded in the contraindications section only (no engine rule). Lithium, digoxin, heparin, ciclosporin and tacrolimus interactions are likewise section-only (not in the master list). Triple combinations (ACE inhibitor + mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist + candesartan/valsartan; ACE inhibitor + beta-blocker + valsartan in heart failure) cannot be expressed as two-drug rules: recorded in cautions; pairwise rules with ACE inhibitors (avoid) and potassium-sparing diuretics carry the main risk. Refractory hypokalaemia/hyponatraemia/hypercalcaemia contraindications (HCTZ combinations) are mapped to the general hypokalaemia/hyponatraemia/hypercalcaemia conditions at contraindicated level; the concern text says "refractory" so the user sees the SmPC scope. NSAID rules: aspirin is given its own rule only for anti-inflammatory doses (SmPCs name acetylsalicylic acid > 3 g/day or at anti-inflammatory dosage); the concern text says low-dose aspirin is not covered. The integrator may prefer to drop these aspirin rules if the engine cannot express dose. Candesartan potassium-sparing diuretic/potassium supplement interactions are monitor-level (candesartan 4.5 says monitor potassium); valsartan, telmisartan and both HCTZ combinations say "not recommended" (avoid). This is a genuine difference between UK SmPCs, not an error. Breastfeeding: SmPCs and MHRA say not recommended (avoid); SPS says ARBs can be used with caution (telmisartan least preferred). Both kept as separate rules for the single ARBs. For the HCTZ combinations only the SmPC/MHRA rule is recorded (SPS page covers ARBs only). Telmisartan SPS: the telmisartan breastfeeding quote "It can be used with caution during breastfeeding if there are specific clinical indications for it." also appears for irbesartan/olmesartan on the same SPS page; context is the telmisartan subsection. Pre-existing issue noticed (not ours): source id sps-macrolides-statins is defined in C.json and E.json with different URLs (sps.nhs.uk vs www.sps.nhs.uk). AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent check, see scripts/medcheck-uk/audit/J-K.md): the five ARB aspirin rules keep level caution but now carry otherFormulations ["aspirin-analgesic"] (the 300 mg analgesic-dose entry added to aspirin.json on 2026-10-17), so they no longer fire for low-dose 75 mg aspirin; concern/action say the warning applies only at anti-inflammatory doses (above 3 g/day for candesartan/valsartan/valsartan-HCTZ). If aspirin-analgesic is renamed or removed, these rules must be updated. Refractory hypercalcaemia concern/action text made explicit (hypokalaemia/hyponatraemia already said refractory). Telmisartan corticosteroid rule limited with otherFormulations to oral prednisolone/dexamethasone (SmPC: systemic route).
